title: A host whose limit is spent is not on Jev's list, and the dispatch says why
name: host-avail
description: `checkHost` in packages/core/src/host.ts answers installed and logged in; it does not answer “can this host take a request right now”, so an account at 100% of its usage window is offered to Jev like any other. Per the `limit-detect` decision, add availability to the host adapter: for `probe`/`probe-and-fall`, a `probe` step that runs one minimal prompt through the host (`claude -p`, `codex exec`, `opencode run`, with the cheapest model the list names for that host) and classifies the exit — ready, limit spent (per-host patterns from captured real output, kept in one table per adapter with the text they were captured from in the test), not logged in, unknown — cached in `.sober/local/hosts.json` under a `dispatch.probeSeconds` TTL (config.ts, default 900). `dispatch()` runs it over the hosts the candidate list names before `askJev` and removes every entry of a host that is not ready; the dispatch log carries one line per removed host with the reason. If nothing is left, refuse before the worktree with all the reasons in one sentence. For `fall` alone, this node ships only the classification (`limitSpent(host, output)`) the fallback node needs, no probe. Tests: host.test.ts per host and per class from captured text; dispatch.test.ts for the filter, the cache TTL and the empty-list refusal.
